title: Risk-proportional review plan (review-plan)
description: Names the reviewer roster and read scope for one review pass, so the pipeline buys review proportional to a logged risk estimate rather than running the full battery on every change. Two authors emit it. scripts/grading.py review-plan (author 'review-plan-engine') is the deterministic estimator: run by the feature-implementer as the final step of gate-pass, it classifies the change set and slice history and either decides the clear cases (risk 'low' with a surface-matched roster, or 'high' with the full roster) or defers the genuine middle to the planner (risk 'gray', no roster). On 'gray', route dispatches the review-planner agent (author 'review-planner'), which reads the diff and appends the final plan with risk 'low' or 'high' and a roster — only the engine may emit 'gray', so triage terminates in one hop. The full battery is the fail-closed default: absent this record, or on any null feature, route dispatches the whole roster (reproducing pre-plan behavior). The 'basis' object carries the facts the estimate was made from — the grader-features pattern — so the planner judges pre-extracted data and every roster is auditable after the fact. See the review-workflow skill § Risk-Proportional Roster.

author.description: 'review-plan-engine' for the deterministic estimator (grading.py review-plan); 'review-planner' for the gray-zone judgment agent. Only the engine may emit risk 'gray'; a 'review-planner' record with risk 'gray' fails Gate 5 and bounces.

risk.description: The estimated review risk. 'low' — a surface-matched subset reviews; 'high' — the full roster reviews (fail-closed default); 'gray' — the engine could not decide, so route dispatches the review-planner to resolve it. A record with risk 'gray' carries no roster.

roster.description: The reviewers to dispatch for this pass. Present for 'low' and 'high'; absent for 'gray' (the planner supplies it). Each name is a floor reviewer or a declared '*-reviewer' extra. The gate for this pass waits on exactly this roster.

scope.description: What the dispatched reviewers read. 'full-diff' — the whole change set under review (first pass). 'fix-delta' — only the fix hunks since the previous review-plan's tree, plus each reviewer's own open findings (re-review cycles), read via scripts/changeset.sh --base-tree.

basis.description: The facts the estimate was made from — deterministic, extracted by the engine so the planner never mines the log and every roster is auditable. Diff-derived fields are null when the base ref does not resolve or the snapshot fails (which forces risk 'high'); handoff-derived fields are null when the log is absent.

tree_sha.description: The content-addressed tree SHA of the working-tree snapshot this plan was computed over — the right-hand side of the change set diff and the anchor a later plan diffs against to compute its fix delta. Null when the snapshot failed. A bare hex object name: the consumer resolves it through git before any diff, so a non-hex value can never reach a git operand.

pass.description: 'first' — no prior review-plan since the latest design-block, so the whole change set is under review. 'fix' — a prior plan exists, so this pass reviews the delta against it.

prev_tree_sha.description: The tree_sha of the prior review-plan this fix pass diffs against. Null on a first pass. Hex object name; the consumer resolves it through git before diffing.

rationale.description: One line stating why this roster and scope. From the engine, a deterministic summary of the deciding facts (the triggers, or the matched surfaces). From the planner, its judgment in one sentence.
